quotes.text: Build a customized payments integration in your iOS, Android, or React Native app using the Payment Element.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: The Payment Element is a customizable component that renders a list of payment methods that you can add into any screen in your app.
A SetupIntent flow allows you to save payment methods for future payments without creating a charge.
Use the [Payment Intents API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents.md) to save payment details from a purchase.
When used with a SetupIntent, PaymentSheet supports cards and PayPal.

historical_claims_to_preserve: April 22 documents in-app embedded payment-method rows with detail sheets and a default Continue return to checkout on iOS and Android, optional in-sheet confirmation for iOS/Android, and mode-dependent backend creation of PaymentIntent for charging, SetupIntent for saving without a charge, or PaymentIntent with future usage to pay and save. Preserve server-determined price, matching client IntentConfiguration, and use of mode-appropriate client secrets/callbacks (old 98–114, 293–330, 579–610, 1189–1199, 1794–1823, 2380–2405, 3035–3041, 3861–3868, 4155–4186 and 5027–5056).

Dated customer passages distinguish Accounts v2 customer-configured Account and `customer_account` from Customers v1 Customer and `customer`; Accounts v2 is described as GA for Connect and public preview with a preview API version for other Stripe users. Saved-card CustomerSession identity and secret are separate from the Intent, with payment_method_save used for the checkbox. Future-use consent, redisplay, later off-session PaymentIntent, and possible authentication errors are separate boundaries (old 794–828, 1277–1311, 1958–2008 and 2380–2405).

Dated follow-up and setup routes should retain the iOS/React Native-on-iOS custom scheme for SDK authentication returns, the desktop-independent platform UI distinctions, and the default opt-out of delayed methods. The `allowsDelayedPaymentMethods` control does not activate methods, and a completed client result can precede the trusted server payment event. PaymentIntent `processing` denotes pending and may later succeed or fail. Keep examples, SDK versions, native Apple Pay and Android Google Pay setup/test qualifications as dated (old 680–759, 905–929, 3825–3845, 4409–4470, 6504–6536 and 6890–6950).

Global pay-and-save `setup_future_usage` and the individual payment method SDK preview represent different dated paths. The preview says to leave both server-level and per-method values unset on the PaymentIntent and let the SDK populate them from its configuration (old 3035–3104, 3320–3376, 6046–6107 and 9196–9280).

April Android examples show `false` for the Android builder, which does not resolve the Swift discrepancy (old 548–576, 1763–1792, 2979–3008 and 4136–4154). Record a source warning and route the concept’s mandate reference to it.

The April iOS setup prose names a SetupIntent from the server and then says the Element confirms a PaymentIntent. Use the setup variant identity and same-variant setup-mode/server descriptions, supported by explicit Android and React Native SetupIntent confirmation, and label the contradictory April iOS wording as historical (old 1189–1199, 1336–1347, 1535–1537, 1724–1726, 1817–1889, 4939–4957 and 7833–7835). Do not take the Android setup example’s payment words as a charge (old 4939–4975).

The concept’s confirmation-control shorthand and mandate source link need scope (wiki/concepts/stripe-inapp-payments.md lines 14–24 and 90–101). The historically documented app-controlled default and optional iOS/Android in-sheet confirmation coexist, and the dated embedded iOS SDK callback uses a custom scheme, distinct from separate app-to-web Universal Link flows described at concept lines 83–84 and 107–110 (old 100–106, 579–601, 680–745, 4155–4179, 6890–6950).

The concept says consent collection automatically handles compliance at line 67. In this dated embedded save flow the merchant is responsible for compliance, explicit use-specific consent and written agreement records, with `allow_redisplay` distinguishing whether attached methods may be shown (old 2395–2405, 3198–3206 and 8554–8565). CustomerSession features enable UI controls and cannot establish compliance. Qualify the concept and reciprocally link the source guidance.

Qualify the generic server-side per-method example at wiki/concepts/stripe-inapp-payments.md lines 42–54 and add a reciprocal warning on the embedded source route at line 97. The April standard global pay-and-save example sets `setup_future_usage` on the server PaymentIntent and matches the client IntentConfiguration. For the separate April embedded SDK per-method preview, leave both `setup_future_usage` and `payment_method_options[X][setup_future_usage]` unset on the server PaymentIntent so the SDK supplies the settings from IntentConfiguration. The concept’s generic server-side per-method example applies outside that documented preview path (old 3035–3067, 3320–3354, 6046–6084 and 9196–9258).

For a reader asking how to set up rather than charge, or how to mount the Element in Android or React Native, route to the nine dated April variants and distinguish SetupIntent from PaymentIntent and the server/webhook boundary (old 10–20, 293–330, 604–610, 747–759, 1189–1199, 2380–2405, 3870–4020, 4940–4975, 6544–6650 and 7453–7457). Current summary lines 16–19 and 59–76 need platform and mode scope. The dated iOS guide requires a scrollable container such as UIScrollView in UIKit or ScrollView in SwiftUI, and passes presentingViewController and delegate in UIKit. Android classic views use ComposeView and the Element content must be scrollable. The Android cart example invokes configure again, while UIKit/SwiftUI and React Native use update; React Native’s native Android view must remain mounted. The iOS form-sheet example optionally confirms the chosen flow immediately after a customer action, with the result callback after dismissal and no reuse after completion, while setup mode immediately confirms setup without charging (old 110–146, 264–286, 333–406, 579–601, 1794–1815, 3899–4016, 4155–4179, 6612–6616 and 6683–6690).

Current summary lines 68–86 omit that confirmation and the UI result can precede an asynchronous payment’s outcome. Distinguish setup completion, delayed payment processing, success and failure. Keep trusted server price calculation and matched IntentConfiguration, server confirmation or SDK confirmation as appropriate to the documented path, and payment fulfillment decisions on server-side events rather than the app result. Preserve mandate placement and working links if rendered manually (old 320–328, 548–576, 604–610, 747–759 and 905–929).

Current summary line 55 uses `.billing_details` as though it were a verified Swift property. The dated UIKit guide supports access to billing details in prose but does not specify that identifier at old lines 249–260. Retain the concept, omit the unverified spelling.

Current summary line 13 presents full cross-platform coverage but gives no targeted route to two April prerequisites. In the setup and pay-and-save variants, attach the payment method for future payment to the object that represents the customer, either an Accounts v2 customer-configured Account or a Customers v1 Customer. On React Native iOS, Stripe cannot present payment methods that require a return URL when one is missing, even if they are enabled. This dated SDK route uses a custom URL scheme forwarded to Stripe (old 1277–1288, 2489–2500, 6890–6900, 7537–7548, 7900–7910 and 8992–9002).

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/accept-payment-embedded, new raw lines 5-24 describe a native Mobile Payment Element integration and route iOS, Android and React Native to payment, setup and payment-plus-setup variants. The index itself specifies neither credentials nor server operations or payment outcomes. The April 22 capture describes the embedded selection UI and detail sheets, the SDK and publishable key, enabled methods, and server endpoints creating a matching PaymentIntent for a charge or a SetupIntent for no-charge setup. For pay-and-save, the PaymentIntent carries the intended future-use setting, with explicit consent for that use. The April setup and pay-and-save variants require attaching the payment method for future payment to a customer-configured Accounts v2 Account or a Customers v1 Customer. The paths use customer_account and customer respectively, with dated Accounts v2 availability and version conditions (old raw lines 1277-1288, old raw lines 2489-2500, old raw lines 7537-7548). In the documented React Native iOS flow, enabled methods that require a return URL are unavailable to users when the app omits it. The guide calls for forwarding the custom-scheme return to the Stripe SDK (old raw lines 6890-6900, old raw lines 7900-7910, old raw lines 8992-9002). CustomerSession options for saved methods are distinct from the Intent, and the documented trusted server amount, Intent client secret, callback or confirmation, processing, success and failure are separate stages (old raw lines 8-114, old raw lines 293-330, old raw lines 604-610, old raw lines 747-759, old raw lines 794-836, old raw lines 1189-1311, old raw lines 2380-2405, old raw lines 3035-3067). The sole mapped source-stripe-inapp-accept-payment-embedded.md preserves useful April UIKit/SwiftUI UI patterns at source lines 13–96 but is largely iOS-oriented and omits platform/mode routing, those attachment and return URL prerequisites, and the asynchronous outcome boundary.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/accept-payment-embedded, new raw lines 5-24 replace the inline guide surface with platform/use-case navigation. This adds a useful route to nine bodies and provides no substantive SDK/API or eligibility delta. Preserve the April 22 capture, its server/client Intent and Account/Customer identities, optional in-sheet confirmation, custom URL-scheme iOS authentication return, delayed-method opt-in, and server-side processing/succeeded/failed distinction (old raw lines 548-610, old raw lines 680-759, old raw lines 905-929, old raw lines 1277-1311, old raw lines 1535-1537, old raw lines 1817-1889, old raw lines 3320-3354, old raw lines 4136-4179, old raw lines 6612-6616). Correct source-stripe-inapp-accept-payment-embedded.md lines 13–19 and 68–86 and qualify its reciprocal concept route. In particular, flag the April Swift mandate snippets using true against prose telling implementers to disable built-in display when rendering their own mandate with working links near Buy, and preserve the SetupIntent/server evidence against the iOS setup paragraph’s stray PaymentIntent wording. At wiki/concepts/stripe-inapp-payments.md lines 42–54 and the reciprocal source entry at line 97, qualify the generic server-side per-method example. Keep the April standard global pay-and-save route, whose server sets setup_future_usage on the PaymentIntent and matches the client IntentConfiguration. For the separate April embedded SDK per-method preview, the server must leave both setup_future_usage and payment_method_options[X][setup_future_usage] unset on the PaymentIntent. The SDK supplies the settings from IntentConfiguration (old raw lines 3035-3067, old raw lines 3320-3354, old raw lines 6046-6084, old raw lines 9196-9258). Preserve use-specific merchant consent responsibilities. An in-app result or browser return cannot establish final payment success, funds availability or compliance, and the unread November variant destinations do not renew April details.
